A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BioBO and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The original experiments and appendix material can be matched reliably despite relocation and expansion in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D report original retrospective BO experiments, sensitivity analyses and biological enrichment results on five GeneDisco assays.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds fusion, runtime, robustness and interpretability experiments. Its explicit clarification that evaluation is retrospective does not negate these original computational results.

M1.justification: Beyond v1's input concatenation and separate GO/Hallmark priors, v2 introduces modality-specific projections followed by latent concatenation or cross-attention (Appendix F), an averaged GO–Hallmark prior (M), and KNN imputation for missing embeddings (K). These extend the model and processing procedures while retaining the core acquisition formula.

E1.justification: The same five phenotype datasets and original embedding resources remain. Appendices J–K add IFN-γ scenarios with mismatched oncology pathway information and incomplete embedding availability, extending input conditions. The new IL-2 interpretability analysis uses an already evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: The original acquisition comparators, including UCB, EI, TS, random selection, enrichment-only selection and DiscoBAX, are retained in their corresponding comparisons. Table 3 adds latent concatenation and latent attention as evaluated surrogate alternatives to the Bayesian-MLP reference, providing a limited expansion of comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix B replaces the stated Gaussian-weight-prior and observation-noise specification with MC dropout at rate 0.5; this establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun. Added protocols include architecture comparisons, enrichment thresholds from 5% to 50%, A10 runtime measurement, and a missing-modality evaluation using 18,344 genes beyond the original complete-embedding restriction.

E4.justification: v1 already includes modality comparisons, beta/aggregation sensitivity and surrogate-quality correlations. Appendices F–O substantially extend analysis with fusion and prior-ensemble comparisons, runtime profiling, top-k threshold sensitivity, mismatched-prior and missing-modality robustness, IL-2 and underexplored-gene case studies, and correlations conditioned on acquisition and fusion strategy.

E5.justification: The original seven-seed, mean-plus-SEM reporting remains. v2 adds a mean-plus-1.96-SEM presentation of the main results in Table 12, while Table 3 specifies standard deviations over five seeds and Appendix K specifies standard deviations over seven seeds. These are reporting additions, not evidence of increased replication of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in original Tables 1–2 and the retained figures are unchanged. Tables 3–11 add architecture, runtime, sensitivity, robustness, enrichment, ensemble and conditional-correlation outcomes. For example, Table 3 newly reports IFN-γ BioUCB-HM recall of 0.127 with latent attention; this concerns a new architecture rather than an updated original score.

T1.justification: The acquisition mathematics and no-harm argument, including Equations 7–8, are unchanged. v2 adds a pointer to the original πBO paper for conditions and proofs, but supplies no new proof, revised assumption or theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the central efficiency, multimodal modeling and interpretability claims. The conclusion additionally claims graceful fallback under mismatched pathways, robustness with missing embeddings, and benefits from combining enrichment sources, extending the claimed practical applicability.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly clarifies retrospective evaluation and substantially expands explanations of local surrogate quality, pathway mismatch, parameter choices, missing embeddings and gene-specific biological mechanisms. Some new interpretations overreach: Appendix I claims uniformly stronger enrichment, although Table 6 reports weaker E2F and G2M significance and combined scores for BioUCB-HM.

D1.justification: v2 revises the surrogate/inference description, changes reported L4 memory from 20 to 24 GB, explicitly documents 20 genes per cycle and 20 cycles, and identifies A10 hardware for timing. It also describes latent-fusion processing and KNN imputation and adds a code-release-on-acceptance statement without an access link.

R1.justification: Section 5 broadens positioning from external knowledge in BO to domain-informed architectures and Bayesian priors in drug discovery. Additional references support retrospective evaluation, assay provenance and biological interpretations; the central relationship to πBO and prior perturbation-design work remains intact.

P1.justification: The original main narrative and section order largely remain, with targeted grammar edits and expanded explanations. v2 adds a computational-efficiency subsection, reproducibility and LLM-use statements, and new appendices; old Appendix D becomes E. Author affiliations, contribution notes and conference headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands tabular presentation with architecture, runtime, robustness, pathway and conditional-correlation tables. Table 12 redisplays Table 1 with expanded uncertainty intervals. All twelve original figure graphics are retained, while Figure 4, Table 2 and appendix material move and some captions change.

improvement.justification: The added runtime, robustness and conditional-correlation analyses make practical behavior more assessable than in v1. Reporting problems limit the gain: Table 3 describes its reference as single-modal although its scores match Table 1's Fusion column, and Table 9's GenePT ensemble score of 0.093 is below the individual-prior scores of 0.095 and 0.096 despite claims of consistent superiority. The broader evidence therefore yields a limited net improvement.
